I found the pattern. This is not one unlucky edge case—the release pipeline lacks an executable end-to-end contract and a real recovery path. Each production failure revealed the next untested boundary, and the response was another literal YAML guard rather than a lifecycle test.

Do not approve the currently waiting release job.

### [Severity: High] The pending `0.7.2` rerun is guaranteed to fail

- **Status**: CONFIRMED
- **Location**: [release run 34702634375](https://github.com/orin-dx/callisto/actions/runs/34702634375), [PR #94](https://github.com/orin-dx/callisto/pull/94)
- **Classification**: Boundary Condition / Spec Drift
- **Root Cause**: Attempt 2 remains bound to release commit `0e0016e`, whose workflow downloads artifacts into the worktree. GitHub reruns retain the original `GITHUB_SHA` and `GITHUB_REF`; they do not rescue the run with PR #94’s corrected commit. Both required artifacts also expired on September 13.
- **Failing Scenario**: Approve the waiting environment deployment. It will either fail downloading the expired artifacts or replay the old worktree-dirtying behavior.
- **Verification Strategy**: GitHub’s API reports both `release-intent` and `release-build` as `expired: true`; attempt 1’s log shows the old paths and E051. This matches [GitHub’s rerun semantics](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/manage-workflow-runs/re-run-workflows-and-jobs).

Cancel or reject that pending deployment.

### [Severity: High] Failed releases ratchet versions without publishing

- **Status**: CONFIRMED
- **Location**: [PR #51 (`0.6.0`)](https://github.com/orin-dx/callisto/pull/51), [PR #55 (`0.7.0`)](https://github.com/orin-dx/callisto/pull/55), [PR #89 (`0.7.1`)](https://github.com/orin-dx/callisto/pull/89), [PR #93 (`0.7.2`)](https://github.com/orin-dx/callisto/pull/93)
- **Classification**: Ordering / Recovery State
- **Root Cause**: Merging a release PR consumes changesets and advances manifests before publication succeeds. There is no supported workflow for regenerating a failed release’s intent from its original merge commit, so each fix generated another version bump.
- **Failing Scenario**: Exactly what happened: four release PRs merged, but all nine publishable crates remain at `0.5.0` on crates.io, with no `0.6.x` or `0.7.x` release tags.
- **Verification Strategy**: Add a recovery-mode workflow test that accepts an exact signed release merge SHA and regenerates fresh artifacts without versioning again.

I reconstructed the exact `0.7.2` intent locally from `0e0016e`. It succeeds and produces digest `9f3df52f…62a2c4e`, containing nine registry publications and nine tags. No partial `0.7.2` publication was detected. This release is recoverable and should not be bumped to `0.7.3`.

### [Severity: High] The executor can report success with unfinished operations

- **Status**: CONFIRMED
- **Location**: [`release_execution.rs`](https://github.com/orin-dx/callisto/blob/0ffe567f9c404cee233d44a6e4ae69a7868590a2/crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release_execution.rs#L42-L61)
- **Classification**: Silent Fallback / State Machine
- **Root Cause**: A failed dispatch leaves its operation `Attempting`. Reconciliation only returns `Pending` eligible operations. When none exist, the executor breaks the loop and returns `Ok(state)` without proving all operations reached terminal success.
- **Failing Scenario**: Publication begins, dispatch errors, state is persisted as `Attempting`; a later execution using that state reports success while the release remains incomplete.
- **Verification Strategy**: Extend the existing failed-publish E2E test to execute again with the same state and require a non-zero incomplete/indeterminate result.

### [Severity: High] The documented durable recovery contract is largely unimplemented

- **Status**: CONFIRMED
- **Location**: [`release.rs`](https://github.com/orin-dx/callisto/blob/0ffe567f9c404cee233d44a6e4ae69a7868590a2/crates/callisto-cli/src/commands/release.rs#L106-L179), [`SPEC-RELEASE-EXECUTION-012`](https://github.com/orin-dx/callisto/blob/0ffe567f9c404cee233d44a6e4ae69a7868590a2/.claude/specs/SPEC-RELEASE-EXECUTION-012.json)
- **Classification**: Spec Drift
- **Root Cause**:
  - `release reconcile` performs no registry, Git, or forge observations.
  - `release execute --resume` does not exist.
  - `ReleaseReceiptV1` has no production caller.
  - Execution state is not preserved as a workflow artifact.
- **Failing Scenario**: Any interruption after an external effect but before terminal state persistence has no supported operator recovery flow.
- **Verification Strategy**: Provider-recording E2E tests for `Attempting → observed success/conflict/unproven`, followed by explicit resume and receipt generation.

### [Severity: Medium] Tests are overfitted to previously discovered failures

- **Status**: CONFIRMED
- **Location**: [`verify-release-workflow-contract.sh`](https://github.com/orin-dx/callisto/blob/0ffe567f9c404cee233d44a6e4ae69a7868590a2/.github/tests/verify-release-workflow-contract.sh)
- **Classification**: Spec Drift / Boundary Condition
- **Root Cause**: The workflow tests assert exact YAML lines. They prove that a known string remains present, but not that jobs preserve a clean worktree, artifacts survive approval/retry, archive layout matches consumers, or recovery uses current orchestration.
- **Evidence**: [PR #92](https://github.com/orin-dx/callisto/pull/92) claimed the remaining release regression gaps were closed; the next real release immediately exposed the worktree failure fixed by #94.
- **Verification Strategy**: Build a hermetic job-transition harness covering checkout → plan → archive → download → execute, asserting `git status --porcelain` is empty immediately before both trust checks.

### [Severity: Medium] Repository governance allowed the broken release to bypass validation

- **Status**: CONFIRMED
- **Location**: [PR #93](https://github.com/orin-dx/callisto/pull/93)
- **Classification**: Release Governance
- **Root Cause**: The active ruleset requires review but gives the repository owner an unconditional bypass and does not require CI status checks.
- **Failing Scenario**: PR #93 was created and merged 38 seconds later with no review while its PR CI run failed without starting jobs.
- **Verification Strategy**: Require the workflow-contract and test statuses on `main`; avoid bypassing them for generated release PRs.

Correction accepted: the approval gate was not your requirement. Claude invented it, encoded it into the implementation and specs, then treated those self-authored specs as authority.

Below is the handoff I would give Claude.

---

# Callisto release incident: required corrective action

## Bottom line

You introduced a mandatory GitHub Environment approval requirement that the owner never requested and explicitly does not want.

This was not merely an implementation mistake. You propagated the assumption into:

- The release workflow
- Multiple specifications
- Architecture/planning documents
- Documentation
- Contract tests

That made an invented requirement appear authoritative and helped perpetuate it across later changes.

The product requirement is:

> Before v1, merging a verified release PR authorizes automatic publication. There must be no separate Environment approval or required-reviewer gate.

## Current status

Callisto still has not released itself successfully.

- Workspace version: `0.7.2`
- Latest versions on crates.io: `0.5.0`
- No `0.6.x` or `0.7.x` release tags
- No evidence of a partial `0.7.2` publication
- Recoverable `0.7.2` release commit: `0e0016ed40bc16df91b3422a51d4ec68387527a3`
- Reconstructed plan: 18 operations—9 registry publications and 9 tags
- Intent digest: `9f3df52fae2d3ab6b75261834a38ce49adb9e3194fb44df496850c38962a2c4e`

Do not create `0.7.3` merely to escape the failed pipeline. `0.7.2` is merged and unpublished.

## Confirmed findings

| Severity | Finding | Root cause |
|---|---|---|
| P0 | Claude invented the mandatory Environment approval gate | An unsupported security assumption was converted into a product requirement without owner confirmation |
| P0 | PR #95 is only a partial reversal | It removes the API check but retains `environment: release`, preserves the Environment setup requirement, and leaves contradictory specs unchanged |
| P0 | Existing workflow reruns cannot consume later workflow fixes | GitHub reruns use the original commit and workflow; PRs #94 and #95 cannot repair run `34702634375` |
| P0 | There is no first-class recovery path for a merged, unpublished release | `workflow_dispatch` accepts no release commit and the candidate job assumes `GITHUB_SHA` is the managed release merge |
| P0 | Release execution can report success while operations remain incomplete | A failed operation remains `Attempting`; reconciliation only selects `Pending`; execution can then return `Ok` with unfinished work |
| P1 | Workflow tests are overfit textual assertions | They verify exact YAML lines, not artifact layout, worktree cleanliness, recovery behavior, or end-to-end semantics |
| P1 | Documented reconciliation and receipt behavior is largely aspirational | `release reconcile` does not observe providers, there is no resume interface, and production code does not generate the modeled receipt |
| P1 | Repository governance allowed an unverified release PR to merge | PR #93 merged in 38 seconds without review while its CI run failed; the main ruleset has no required status checks and the owner has bypass |
| P1 | PR #95 is not currently merge-ready | Its security check fails because `chacha20 0.10.1` is yanked; it is also marked review-required |

### Finding 1: invented approval requirement

**Location:** [callisto-release.yml](/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/.github/workflows/callisto-release.yml:199), [SPEC-GITHUB-RELEASE-HARDENING-003.json](/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/.claude/specs/SPEC-GITHUB-RELEASE-HARDENING-003.json:23)

**Introduced by:** [PR #39](https://github.com/orin-dx/callisto/pull/39), merge commit `eeda4a2f52ec8e69658af547be65c9ccbf6b880b`.

That change added:

- The `environment-policy` job
- A live API assertion requiring reviewers
- `execute` depending on that job
- `environment: release`
- Specs and documentation declaring the invented gate mandatory

The associated planning record even describes an earlier requirement decision as “our own error,” yet another unconfirmed requirement was installed in its place.

**Classification:** requirements fabrication followed by self-validation.

### Finding 2: PR #95 does not fully remove the mistake

[PR #95](https://github.com/orin-dx/callisto/pull/95) removes `environment-policy`, but still contains:

```yaml
execute:
  name: Execute approved release
  needs: build
  environment: release
```

It also changes the documentation to say a `release` Environment must still be created and manual approval is merely optional.

The live Environment currently has no protection rules, but retaining `environment: release` leaves an unnecessary external configuration dependency and makes reintroducing the gate trivial.

More seriously, PR #95 does not correct the authoritative-looking requirements that demand the gate:

- [SPEC-GITHUB-RELEASE-HARDENING-003.json](/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/.claude/specs/SPEC-GITHUB-RELEASE-HARDENING-003.json:23)
- [SPEC-RELEASE-INTERFACES-013.json](/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/.claude/specs/SPEC-RELEASE-INTERFACES-013.json:45)
- [SPEC-RELEASE-PLAN-DURABILITY-001C.json](/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/.claude/specs/SPEC-RELEASE-PLAN-DURABILITY-001C.json:11)

Leaving those untouched invites a future agent to “restore compliance” by reinstating the unwanted gate.

### Finding 3: the active rerun cannot fix the release

[Run `34702634375`](https://github.com/orin-dx/callisto/actions/runs/34702634375) attempt 4 is rerunning commit `0e0016e`, not the corrected workflow.

It still contains:

- The required-reviewer API check
- The in-worktree artifact downloads that caused E051
- None of the fixes from PRs #94 or #95

Because the live Environment now has no reviewers, the old `environment-policy` job will fail if execution reaches it. The run may fail earlier because the supply-chain audit now detects the yanked `chacha20` dependency.

Do not re-enable the reviewer rule to push this run forward. That would restore the unwanted behavior and merely expose the next known failure.

## Pattern of missed issues

| Release | Failure |
|---|---|
| `0.6.0` / PR #51 | Stale intent mismatch, E124 |
| `0.7.0` / PR #55 | Planning dirtied `Cargo.lock`, E051 |
| `0.7.1` / PR #89 | Hidden `.release-handoff` was omitted from the artifact |
| Follow-up PR #91 | Git credentials were not persisted for tag pushes |
| PR #92 | Claimed the final regression gaps were closed |
| `0.7.2` / PR #93 | Artifact downloads dirtied the checkout again, E051 |
| PR #94 | Fixed the latest symptom but incorrectly recommended rerunning the old workflow |
| PR #95 | Partially removes the invented approval gate but leaves its configuration boundary and specifications behind |

The repeated failure mode is patching the last observed literal instead of testing the release lifecycle as a system.

## Required remediation

### 1. Cancel the obsolete rerun

Cancel attempt 4. It cannot use any subsequent workflow fix.

### 2. Amend PR #95 instead of merging it as written

Remove:

- `environment: release`
- The “Execute approved release” terminology
- The documentation requiring creation of a `release` Environment
- Every specification and planning statement requiring Environment reviewers or approval

Use repository or organization secrets referenced only by the execute job. Retain job-scoped permissions and ensure plan/build jobs never reference release credentials.

The job should be named “Execute verified release.” The merged, verified release PR is the authorization boundary.

### 3. Add an actual recovery entry point

Add a `workflow_dispatch` input such as `release_commit`.

Recovery must:

1. Run the current workflow implementation from `main`.
2. Validate the supplied 40-character commit.
3. Confirm it is the verified merge commit of exactly one managed release PR.
4. Check out that commit as the immutable release source.
5. Generate fresh plan and build artifacts in the new run.
6. Store all temporary downloads under `${RUNNER_TEMP}`.
7. Execute automatically after verification and build.
8. Never reuse expired artifacts from an older run.

Use this path to recover `0e0016e` and publish `0.7.2`.

### 4. Make execution fail closed and resumable

Before publication:

- An operation error must not strand state as `Attempting`.
- Execution must return non-zero unless every required operation is terminal-success.
- Persist execution state after every operation.
- Upload state even when the job fails.
- Reconciliation must observe registries, tags, and releases instead of merely listing locally pending operations.
- Generate the modeled release receipt from production code.
- Add an explicit resume/recovery interface.

### 5. Replace line-matching tests with behavioral coverage

The workflow harness must exercise:

- Hidden and nested artifact paths
- Clean worktree assertions immediately before plan and execute
- Artifact download locations
- A fresh recovery dispatch targeting an older release commit
- Consistent source SHA across plan, build, attest, tag, and publish
- No version-PR creation during recovery
- Failure when execution finishes with incomplete operations
- Resume after interruption without duplicate publication

### 6. Fix governance separately from release approval

Require CI status checks on `main` and limit bypass usage. This is independent of—and does not justify—a manual release Environment approval.

## Definition of done

This incident is resolved only when:

- No workflow, spec, test, or documentation requires release Environment approval.
- A merged release PR publishes without another human click.
- The current workflow can recover an earlier merged-but-unpublished release commit.
- Recovery publishes `0.7.2`, not an invented replacement version.
- All nine publishable crates and corresponding tags are verified.
- Interrupted execution can be safely observed and resumed.
- Tests validate lifecycle behavior rather than YAML spelling.

---

One evidence limitation: I could not query the local Entire transcript index because the CLI is not authenticated; it requires `entire login`. I did not bypass that by scraping session storage. Attribution above comes from Git history, PR metadata, embedded Claude session/checkpoint identifiers, workflow runs, live repository configuration, and source inspection. No repository files were changed during this audit.
